scope: Long-term disposition of the tests/Hexalith.Conversations.Conformance.Tests -> src/Hexalith.Conversations.Server project reference and the conformance oracle's tier structure.

closesActionItem.action: Decide the long-term path for residual Conformance.Tests to Server coupling.

supersedes.supersededText: Public-surface suites no longer transitively depend on the Server plumbing assembly.
supersedes.reason: The target end-state was written when Hexalith.Conversations.Server held the plumbing being refactored out by Epics 2-3. That plumbing has since moved to Hexalith.EventStore.DomainService, Hexalith.Commons.*, and platform deployment. What remains in Server is Conversations-owned decision code that the Epic 6 corrected ownership spine assigns to the module and that must not become public. The end-state as written is therefore no longer the correct target, and retaining it would keep an unmeetable promise on the record.

decisionSummary: The residual coupling is a mislabeling, not a defect. The oracle asserts two different contracts and has never distinguished them. Declare two tiers, make the portable tier's property structural and test-asserted, and stop pursuing removal of a reference whose original justification has expired.

rejectedAlternatives.option: Publicize Server seams and delete the project reference
rejectedAlternatives.rejectedBecause: Widens the 196-type public contract solely for test reachability, triggering FR-20 contract-shape approval and permanently worsening the adopter surface to solve a test-structure problem.

rejectedAlternatives.option: Accept the coupling permanently with no structural change
rejectedAlternatives.rejectedBecause: Leaves the architecture's adopter-verifiability intent unmeetable for the whole oracle and keeps the portable/coupled distinction as prose, which is exactly the form that let this item be deferred three times.
Story 6.6 is last and must attest on current evidence. An open Architect/Quality decision at attestation time is the failure mode Epic 6 exists to correct.

portable.assertedBy: structural test over the resolved compile surface

invariants: Tier membership governs what an assertion may bind, never whether it runs.
Widening the public contract to relocate an assertion is prohibited.
Weakening an assertion to relocate it is a conformance failure.
Executed conformance test count is monotonic across both tiers.
The pre-split count is derived from a machine-readable result artifact, never transcribed.

fr20Reclassification.obligationText: Removing, replacing, or reclassifying any manifested test requires explicit named-owner approval, rationale, replacement evidence where applicable, and a versioned manifest update; no conformance test is silently dropped.

triageInput.note: Input set only. Per-file outcomes are emitted by Story 6.9, never hand-authored.

permittedAlternateOutcome: If the triage proves the coupled assertions re-express against public surfaces at unchanged strength, a single portable project with the reference removed is a valid successful result. This decision commits to tiering the oracle, not to producing two projects.
nonClaims: This decision does not assert the split has been executed.
This decision does not assert any file is re-expressible; the triage decides.
This decision does not waive, weaken, or reduce the FR-20 denominator.
This decision does not authorize any production source change.
This decision does not edit, mutate, or reinterpret any immutable v1 evidence artifact.
